newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: MOST CZECHS SEE THEMSLEVES AS RIGHT-WING - SURVEY.
newsitem.headline: MOST CZECHS SEE THEMSLEVES AS RIGHT-WING - SURVEY.

text.p: Most Czechs see themselves on the right side of the political spectrum, a survey released on Monday by a state-run Institute for Public opinion (IVVM) showed.
The early November sample of 1,001 Czechs showed 37 percent claiming to be "rightists", 21 percent were "leftists", while 32 percent said they were "centrists".
Among those seeing themselves as rightists, 17 percent said they belonged to the centre-right, 17 percent said they were simply rightists, and three percent said they were ultra-right.
Of those seeing themselves as left-wing, 14 said they belonged to the centre-left, five percent simply left and two percent were far-left.
The country has had a centrist or centre-right coalition government since the fall of communism in 1989.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's conservative coalition lost its parliamentary majority in June general elections, but won a majority of Senate seats in recent upper house elections.
